items.subject: english
items.question: How many volunteers had failed to update the noticeboard before the committee added the confirmation step?
items.passage: A fictional garden committee published a watering roster on a noticeboard. When a volunteer could not attend, that person was asked to arrange a replacement and update the board. After two missed sessions, the committee learned that replacements had been arranged but the board had not been changed. Other volunteers therefore believed the slots were empty and duplicated the work. The committee added a simple confirmation step: the replacement would initial the revised slot. The adjustment addressed the recording of responsibility rather than imposing an additional watering session. The report did not attribute the duplication to volunteers being unwilling to help.

excerpts.text: A fictional garden committee published a watering roster on a noticeboard. When a volunteer could not attend, that person was asked to arrange a replacement and update the board. After two missed sessions, the committee learned that replacements had been arranged but the board had not been changed. Other volunteers therefore believed the slots were empty and duplicated the work. The committee added a simple confirmation step: the replacement would initial the revised slot. The adjustment addressed the recording of responsibility rather than imposing an additional watering session. The report did not attribute the duplication to volunteers being unwilling to help.

items.explanation: The passage refers to two missed sessions in which the board had not been changed, so two volunteers had failed to update it.

items.subject: accountancy
items.question: According to the significance of the current ratio, a very high current ratio is associated with which of the following?

options.text: Under-utilisation or improper utilisation of resources
Risk of being unable to pay short-term debt on time

excerpts.text:
Significance: It provides a measure of degree to which current assets cover current
liabilities. The excess of current assets over current liabilities provides a measure
of safety margin available against uncertainty in realisation of current assets
and flow of funds. The ratio should be reasonable. It should neither be very high
or very low. Both the situations have their inherent disadvantages. A very high
current ratio implies heavy investment in current assets which is not a good
sign as it reflects under utilisation or improper utilisation of resources. A low
ratio endangers the business and puts it at risk of facing a situation where it
will not be able to pay its short-term debt on time. If this problem persists, it
may affect firm’s credit worthiness adversely. Normally, it is safe to have this
ratio within the range of 2:1.

items.explanation: A very high current ratio implies heavy investment in current assets. A risk of not paying short-term debt on time and current liabilities exceeding current assets are features of a low current ratio.

items.subject: accountancy
items.question: Debentures that can be converted into equity shares at the option of the company or the debenture holders are called:

excerpts.text:
2.3.3 From the Point of view of Convertibility
(a) Convertible Debentures: Debentures which are convertible into equity
shares or in any other security either at the option of the company or
the debentureholders are called convertible debentures. These
debentures are either fully convertible or partly convertible.
(b) Non-Convertible Debentures: The debentures which cannot be
converted into shares or in any other securities are called non-
convertible debentures. Most debentures issued by companies fall in
this category.

2.3.2 From the Point of view of Tenure
(a) Redeemable Debentures: Redeemable debentures are those which
are payable on the expiry of the specific period either in lump sum
or in Instalments during the life time of the company. Debentures
can be redeemed either at par or at premium.
(b) Irredeemable Debentures: Irredeemable debentures are also known
as Perpetual Debentures because the company does not give any
undertaking for the repayment of money borrowed by issuing such
debentures. These debentures are repayable on the winding-up of a
company or on the expiry of a long period.

items.explanation: Non-convertible debentures are those that can be converted into equity shares at the option of the company or the debenture holders, so option B is correct.

items.subject: economics
items.question: When an Indian resident buys a car company in the United Kingdom, how is this transaction entered in India's capital account?

options.text: As an item in the balance of trade
It is not recorded in the balance of payments

excerpts.text:
6.1.2 Capital Account
Capital Account records all international transactions of assets. An asset is any
one of the forms in which wealth can be held, for example: money, stocks, bonds,
Government debt, etc. Purchase of assets is a debit item on the capital account.
If an Indian buys a UK Car Company, it enters capital account transactions as
a debit item (as foreign exchange is flowing out of India). On the other hand, sale
of assets like sale of share of an Indian company to a Chinese customer is a
credit item on the capital account. Fig. 6.2 classifies the items which are a part
of capital account transactions. These items are Foreign Direct Investments (FDIs),
Foreign Institutional Investments (FIIs), external borrowings and assistance.

items.explanation: Buying a foreign company brings ownership of an asset into India, so it is entered as a credit item on the capital account; option B is correct.

build up of stock of debt and interest liabilities and force the government,

items.explanation: A revenue deficit is the excess of revenue expenditure over revenue receipts. items.subject: english
items.question: Why did the school move one bus departure from 4:00 to 4:15?
items.passage: In a fictional school, a bus timetable was revised after students reported long waits. The school shifted one departure from 4:00 to 4:15, allowing pupils in a late laboratory session to reach it. Pupils whose classes ended earlier consequently waited longer. The school retained an earlier departure on another route and asked students to choose the departure suited to their class schedule. The notice described the revision as a compromise between different finishing times. It neither promised shorter waits for everyone nor described the later departure as a faster journey.

options.text: So that pupils in a late laboratory session could reach that departure
So that every pupil would wait for a shorter time
Because the later departure made the journey faster
Because the earlier route had been cancelled

excerpts.text: In a fictional school, a bus timetable was revised after students reported long waits. The school shifted one departure from 4:00 to 4:15, allowing pupils in a late laboratory session to reach it. Pupils whose classes ended earlier consequently waited longer. The school retained an earlier departure on another route and asked students to choose the departure suited to their class schedule. The notice described the revision as a compromise between different finishing times. It neither promised shorter waits for everyone nor described the later departure as a faster journey.

items.explanation: The passage says the departure was shifted to 4:15, 'allowing pupils in a late laboratory session to reach it'. The notice neither promised shorter waits for everyone nor described the later departure as faster, and the school retained an earlier departure on another route, so B, C and D are not supported.

items.subject: accountancy
items.question: While calculating the quick (acid-test) ratio, which of the following current assets is excluded from quick assets?

excerpts.text:
Current Liabilities
The quick assets are defined as those assets which are quickly convertible
into cash. While calculating quick assets we exclude the inventories at the end
and other current assets such as prepaid expenses, advance tax, etc., from the
current assets. Because of exclusion of non-liquid current assets it is considered
better than current ratio as a measure of liquidity position of the business. It is
calculated to serve as a supplementary check on liquidity position of the business
and is therefore, also known as ‘Acid-Test Ratio’.

Current Liabilities
Current assets include current investments, inventories, trade receivables
(debtors and bills receivables), cash and cash equivalents, short-term loans and
advances and other current assets such as prepaid expenses, advance tax and
accrued income, etc.
Current liabilities include short-term borrowings, trade payables (creditors
and bills payables), other current liabilities and short-term provisions.

items.explanation: Quick assets are those quickly convertible into cash; inventories and other current assets such as prepaid expenses and advance tax are excluded from them. Trade receivables (which include bills receivable) and cash and cash equivalents remain part of quick assets.

items.subject: accountancy
items.question: To secure its debentures, a company creates a charge on all its assets other than those already assigned to secured creditors, instead of on any one specific asset. What kind of charge has the company created?

options.text: No charge, because the debentures are unsecured
A charge only on its inventories

excerpts.text:
2.3.1 From the Point of view of Security
(a) Secured Debentures: Secured debentures refer to those debentures
where a charge is created on the assets of the company for the purpose
of payment in case of default. The charge may be fixed or floating. A
fixed charge is created on a specific asset whereas a floating charge is

on the general assets of the company. The fixed charge is created
against those assets which are held by a company for use in operations
not meant for sale whereas floating charge involves all assets excluding
those assigned to the secured creditors.
(b) Unsecured Debentures: Unsecured debentures do not have a specific
charge on the assets of the company. However, a floating charge may
be created on these debentures by default. Normally, these kinds of
debentures are not issued.

items.explanation: A fixed charge is created on a specific asset held for use in operations, whereas a floating charge covers all the assets excluding those assigned to the secured creditors. A charge on the company's general assets is therefore a floating charge. The debentures are not unsecured, because a charge has been created, and the charge is not limited to inventories.

items.question: Choose the word most nearly OPPOSITE in meaning to INDIFFERENT as used in the sentence: 'Rahul was indifferent to the new science club and never asked a single question about it.'

excerpts.text: having or showing no interest in somebody/something
very interested in learning about many different things
continuing for only a short time
using only as much money or food as is necessary
(of an excuse or explanation) reasonable and likely to be true

items.explanation: Indifferent means having or showing no interest in something. Inquisitive means very interested in learning about many different things, so it is the opposite. Transient (lasting a short time), frugal (using only what is necessary) and plausible (reasonable and likely to be true) are unrelated to interest.

items.subject: economics
items.question: During a year, the value of a country's imports of goods is greater than the value of its exports of goods. Its balance of trade is said to be in:

excerpts.text:
Balance on Current Account has two components:
• ·Balance of Trade or Trade Balance
• ·Balance on Invisibles
Balance of Trade (BOT) is the difference between the value of exports
and value of imports of goods of a country in a given period of time.
Export of goods is entered as a credit item in BOT, whereas import of
goods is entered as a debit item in BOT. It is also known as Trade
Balance.
BOT is said to be in balance when exports of goods are equal to the
imports of goods. Surplus BOT or Trade surplus will arise if country
exports more goods than what it imports. Whereas, Deficit BOT or Trade
deficit will arise if a country imports more goods than what it exports.
Net Invisibles is the difference between the value of exports and value

items.explanation: The balance of trade is the difference between the value of exports and imports of goods. It is in balance when they are equal, in surplus when exports of goods exceed imports, and in deficit when imports of goods exceed exports. The current account also includes invisibles, so a trade deficit does not tell us that the current account is in surplus.
